parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct has ever existed, no traveller-facing universal exposure (document screening, facility bans, registration) is documented, and official posture is welcoming: a tourism-ministry LGBT campaign, a ministry request that media stop mocking LGBT people, Pride since 2003, and a visible scene in two cities. Against that, the dossier documents a real pattern: 135+ street harassment/abuse cases against trans women, 100+ violence incidents reported in 2017, a 2016 survey where ~38% of trans women were arrested (90% for being trans), and a police practice of extorting and abusing trans sex workers in one city. Recourse is thin: no enacted non-discrimination statute, UPR acceptances unimplemented.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border screening, document-mismatch friction, marker rules or refusal-of-entry practice appears in the dossier.
entry_documents.protection: Never criminalised same-sex activity or gender expression; no entry restriction on transgender visitors is recorded.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown whether document presentation triggers secondary inspection; nothing links entry to the documented street or policing exposures.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2016 survey: ~38% of surveyed trans women arrested, over 90% saying because they were transgender (sampling frame unstated). Police in one city targeted trans sex workers with forced bathing, extortion and expulsion.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific offence exists; no imprisonment for gender expression is documented, and custody conditions for trans detainees are not described as abusive.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest risk flows into custody, where placement is surgery-gated per a 2025 praise statement with no policy text; placement for non-surgical detainees is undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: City-level policing variation: documented abusive practice in one city, street-harassment cases recorded across urban centres without city breakdown; scene concentrated in two cities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Pride annually since 2003, first Pride in second city 2018, first gay district in capital — indicating live public space in major cities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor outside the two scene cities loses both the visible support network and any local familiarity with LGBT people.

care_services.exposure: No visitor-facing care denial documented. Gender-affirming surgery not legally available is a resident gap; emergency-care treatment of an outed visitor is unmeasured.
care_services.protection: 2017 foreign government report found no official discrimination in employment, citizenship, education or health care.
care_services.interaction: Prison overcrowding from gang crackdowns could place a detained visitor in degraded facilities without trans-specific protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police practice in one city of targeting transgender sex workers — extortion, forced naked bathing in stagnant water, expulsion — while cisgender sex workers were not treated the same.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Information ministry asked media to stop mocking LGBT people citing constitutional honour; tourism ministry endorsed an LGBT-welcome campaign; cabinet cooperation on paper.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official welcoming posture sits alongside unaddressed police abuse, with no enacted statute to constrain officer conduct.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travellers. Widespread family rejection (81% emotional abuse, 35% suicide ideation) and school bullying describe residents' spheres, not a visiting minor's itinerary.
minors_guardians.protection: School curriculum since 2018 covers gender identity and combating LGBT discrimination; 3,000+ teachers trained.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting minor travelling with a trans adult inherits the adult's street-harassment and policing exposure but faces no documented child-specific rule.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 135+ documented harassment/abuse cases against trans women on city streets; 100+ violence/abuse incidents reported in 2017; a foreign government listed LGBTI violence among most significant human-rights issues.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No official discrimination recorded in services; visible bars and clubs; annual Pride; UN expert visits hosted in 2023.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Harassment exposure is highest where the scene is least visible; national human-rights bodies document but do not appear to intervene.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No non-discrimination provisions in legislation; 2015 cabinet claim of existing protection disputed and unenforceable; 2024 UPR acceptances (self-ID, marriage, anti-discrimination) unenacted.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active national human-rights organisations and a cooperative international posture; UPR recommendations accepted rather than rejected.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Monitoring without enacted law means street and policing harms are recorded but not systematically remedied for a short-stay visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this dossier. Vellandra imposes a universal, enforced Visitor Conduct Register barring transgender entry with no remedy — a state-imposed universal exposure. This jurisdiction documents no entry restriction, no registration, and no traveller-facing exclusion regime; its harms are street harassment and localized police abuse, not an engineered border system.

Comparable. Kestrel Isles shows uneven secondary screening with humiliation, refused admission and slow remedies — friction concentrated at the border. This dossier's friction sits instead in streets and policing, with documented patterned harassment and police abuse, but no criminalisation and a welcoming official climate; roughly the same tier, differently located.

Higher than this dossier. Meridia pairs trained border officers with a working Civil Liberties Tribunal awarding release and compensation for detention. This dossier has comparable absence of criminalisation but no documented functioning remedy for the recorded street violence and police abuse, and unimplemented statutory protections — so it sits a step below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime pairs a genuinely permissive legal baseline (no criminalisation ever, no gender-expression offence, no documented official discrimination in services) and an unusually warm official posture (tourism campaign, media-mockery rebuke, two decades of Pride) with an unremedied street-and-policing layer: patterned harassment of trans women, a documented police practice of extortion and degradation against trans sex workers in one city, and a survey suggesting arrest is common and identity-motivated. No traveller-facing universal exposure is documented, and no border or document rule appears at all. Recourse is thin — acceptances at UN review remain unenacted, so monitoring outpaces law. For a visitor outside sex work, exposure is situational and geographically uneven; if detained, custody placement is surgery-gated and undocumented otherwise. Net: elevated but not high risk, warranting roughly 0.57.
